A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Text, equations, all 11 figures, all 10 tables, and Appendices A-D are readable and matchable. The increase from 17 to 18 pages reflects reflow and reference overflow, without missing comparison material.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark experiments, representation analyses, synthetic experiments, ablations, and repeated-run results in Sections 3-5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark scores, synthetic experiments, ablations, and the three-seed results in Appendix B.4.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same alignment and uniformity losses and integration of target SSL with PDM. Appendix D.4 still specifies SimSiam. The abstract's replacement of alignment/uniformity wording with 'de-collapse techniques' rephrases the existing approach.

E1.justification: Both versions use Office31, OfficeHome, VisDA, DomainNet, and the synthetic toy data. General and extreme UniDA scenarios, label-distribution sweeps, and target-subset evaluations are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within the corresponding experiments, including UAN, CMU, UniOT, DANCE, and MLNet in Tables 3-6 and the SSL alternatives in Table 7. Table 1's revised descriptions concern related work, not newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The H-score metric, label partitions in Table 10, and experimental procedures remain unchanged. Appendix D retains ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50, 10K training steps, batch size 36 per domain, and the same loss weights and toy-experiment settings.

E4.justification: Both retain the singular-value analyses, controlled importance-weight errors, SSL-component ablations, toy visualizations, label-distribution robustness analysis, target-private SSL analysis, and hyperparameter sensitivity study in Sections 3-5 and Appendix B.

E5.justification: Appendix B.4 in both versions reports three runs with different random seeds and standard deviations in Table 8. No run-count, uncertainty-reporting, or statistical-procedure changes are present.

E6.justification: The numerical entries and plotted findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 7 retains H-scores of 72.3, 71.8, and 70.6 for UAN with SimSiam, AlignUniform, and Barlow Twins, respectively.

T1.justification: The label-set definitions, objectives, importance-weight error metric, and Equations 1-16 are retained, as are the appendix definitions. Equation 8 moves across a page boundary without mathematical revision; neither version adds formal proofs.

C1.justification: Both retain the same central claims: extreme UniDA exposes PDM failures caused by target dimensional collapse, target SSL mitigates this problem, and the approach supports broader UniDA coverage. Abstract and contribution-list edits do not change these claims' substance or scope.

C2.justification: The explanations linking collapse to importance-weight errors and distinguishing alignment from uniformity remain unchanged. Both retain the interpretation of stronger benefits in extreme UniDA and Appendix B.2's qualification that SSL on target-private data can have small negative effects.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-page pointer in the abstract and acknowledges NCHC computational and storage support. Appendix D's implementation information is otherwise unchanged. These are disclosure additions; the PDFs do not establish a new code/data release or changed hardware configuration.

R1.justification: Table 1 changes the stated goals of Sun/Xu from 'Minimize domain gap' and Bucci from 'Learn target info' to 'Reduce negative transfer' for both groups. This modestly revises the positioning against prior SSL approaches; the cited works and Appendix A remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 lightly revises the abstract and introduction, adds an opening sentence about distribution shift, removes several qualifiers, and adds acknowledgments and conference publication text. The section organization and almost all explanatory prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 1, 2, and 7 switch from small-cap styling to ordinary capitalization with adjusted sizing. Citation and cross-reference text changes from blue to black, and content reflows across pages. All figures and tables are retained without new graphical evidence.

improvement.justification: The new project-page pointer and funding/computational-support disclosures provide a modest improvement in discoverability and transparency over v2. Scientific evidence, analyses, and implementation settings remain unchanged, so the gain is limited to documentation; the PDFs do not establish additional reproducibility resources.
